title: FROM RETAINED RUN TO SCOPED CHECK
question: What does Eval Evidence do today to a retained evaluation run?
takeaway: It reads retained artifacts, builds a deterministic evidence bundle, and returns scoped integrity results.

reading_speeds.at_2_seconds: One current pipeline turns retained artifacts into a scoped result.
reading_speeds.at_20_seconds: An adapter normalizes evidence, bundle construction records claims and file fingerprints, and verification checks only named integrity surfaces.
reading_speeds.at_2_minutes: The source map and adjacent prose preserve the boundary between recorded evidence, byte identity, and claims the current release does not implement.

medium.rationale: The shipped stage order and proof scope require exact, reviewable labels on desktop and mobile.

labels.claim: Eval Evidence begins from already retained evaluator artifacts.
The selected adapter maps retained values into the framework-neutral normalized model.
Bundle construction records normalized claims and selected file fingerprints deterministically.
Verification checks schema, embedded digest, and optionally referenced local bytes.
Commands report validity and named failures without adjudicating truth or comparability.

boundaries: The current release does not run models or evaluations.
It does not ship a comparison engine or generated publication report.
A successful integrity check does not establish score truth, runner authenticity, or model quality.

accessibility.alt_text: Retained run artifacts pass through evidence normalization and deterministic bundle construction to scoped schema, digest, and referenced-byte checks.
accessibility.long_description: A single left-to-right pipeline has four numbered stages: retained run, normalize evidence, canonical bundle, and scoped check. The last stage emits a scoped JSON result. A small boundary note says the current release records and checks evidence but does not run evaluations, compare models, or establish truth.
